title: Introduce frugality-mode runner and quant-drift watchdog
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Add frugality-mode (opt-in) that provides conservative batching/caching defaults and a quantization drift detector; backward-compatible; new CLI helpers and telemetry added.
description: Title: Introduce frugality-mode runner and quant-drift watchdog. Summary: Adds an opt-in 'frugality' execution mode designed for cost-sensitive tenants. Frugality mode applies conservative batching and cache retention defaults, introduces a simulated shadow-runner to validate cheaper quant profiles before rollout, and a quant-drift watchdog that monitors eval/quality signals for regressions and triggers safe rollback policies. Motivation: customers requested stronger default guardrails for unit economics when enabling low-cost quantized variants. This change bundles deploy-time defaults, a dry-run validator, and runtime telemetry/alerts so teams can safely try tighter cost profiles without manual scaffolding. What changed (high level): 1) runtime/orchestrator: new frugality policy layer that adjusts batch sizing and kv-cache TTLs by tenant tier; 2) runtime/quant: shadow-runner that can run a sample percentage of requests with a candidate quant profile and compare quality metrics; 3) ops/cli: new `rwdctl frugality` subcommands for dry-run, promote, and rollback; 4) telemetry: new metrics and events (frugality.run.sampled, quant.cohort.regression, frugality.policy.applied) and dashboards; 5) safety: automated rollback hooks triggered by quant-drift watchdog when eval thresholds breach; 6) tests: end-to-end smoke harness and unit tests for policy application. Commits (summary): - a1b3c7d: initial frugality policy scaffolding and default profiles; - 9f4e2b1: shadow-runner implementation + sample scheduler; - 2c7d4f9: rwdctl CLI integration and docs; - c3a2f01: telemetry and dashboards; - f5b4a88: tests and CI fixes. Files touched (high-level): - runtime/policy/frugality_policy.go (new) - runtime/quant/shadow_runner.go (new) - cli/rwdctl/frugality_cmd.go (new) - config/defaults/frugality_profiles.yaml (new) - telemetry/metrics_registry.go (updated) - dashboards/cost_guardrails.json (new) - tests/e2e/frugality_smoke_test.go (new) - internal/rollback/quant_watchdog.go (new) - docs/frugality_mode.md (new) - CI: .github/workflows/frugality-ci.yaml (new) Change rationale: We observed several customer incidents where aggressive quant rollouts reduced cost but silently regressed quality for edge prompt families. Frugality mode is a defensive set of defaults and an automated validation loop to lower the blast radius of low-cost configurations while still enabling experimentation. Backwards compatibility: Mode is off by default. Existing tenants see no behavior change unless they opt in via the tenant profile API or CLI. Testing notes: Unit tests cover policy application, sample scheduling, and the watchdog threshold logic. E2E smoke runs a synthetic workload with a golden prompt set and verifies no regression for control vs candidate. CI flow: initial push failed unit tests due to a race in sample scheduler; fixed in commit f5b4a88. All CI checks green on final push. Documentation: Added docs/frugality_mode.md with configuration examples and recommended conservative defaults for small/medium/large tenants. Review conversation (high level and timeline): - Marina Lopez (reviewer) comment at 2026-02-19: "Nice encapsulation; need stronger typing on profile YAML and explicit schema validation to avoid silent misconfigs." Author reply 2026-02-19: "Added YAML schema validation and explicit error messages; see frugality_profiles.yaml and validation tests." - Ethan Brooks (reviewer) requested changes 2026-02-20: "Shadow-runner should not affect production latency; ensure sampling is entirely async and bounded CPU. Also add telemetry for sample throttles." Author reply 2026-02-21: "Made sampling strictly asynchronous, capped CPU/threads, and added telemetry events for throttles (frugality.sample.throttled)." - Chen Wang (reviewer) found an edge-case 2026-02-22: "Watchdog threshold config is per-tenant but fallback global exists — include clear precedence and docs." Author reply 2026-02-22: "Document precedence and implemented explicit merge order (tenant -> tenant-group -> global)." - CI initially: build: pass; unit: fail (flaky sample scheduler race) -> fixed; integration: pass; lint: pass. Final CI status: pass. Approvals: Marina Lopez approved 2026-02-24; Ethan Brooks approved 2026-02-24; Chen Wang approved 2026-02-25. Merge details: Squash merge performed on 2026-02-25 by Priya Shah with commit message "frugality: add runner, shadow validation, quant watchdog, CLI and telemetry (squash)". Deployment notes: Feature gated under runtime flag FRUGALITY_MODE and tenant opt-in API fields. Ops runbook: Added to docs/runbooks/cost-guardrails-runbook.md with steps to enable, monitor frugality.run.sampled, inspect quant.cohort.regression spikes, and how to trigger manual rollback via `rwdctl frugality rollback --tenant <id>`. Observability: Added dashboards/cost_guardrails.json and alerts: - critical if quant.cohort.regression > 0.05 over 5m -> auto rollback trigger (controlled) - warning if sample.throttled rate > 10% over 10m -> notify SRE. Performance expectations: Frugality defaults aim to reduce tail unit-cost by ~12-22% for quant-friendly workloads while targeting <3% quality delta on golden evals; numbers are workload dependent. Migration and compatibility: No migration necessary for existing tenants. New profile file contains sample conservative presets for nv4x, v100x, and aarch64 inference nodes. Security: Shadow-runner executes only on anonymized request copies; no PII retained; passes threat modeling review. Follow-ups and TODOs: - Add tenant-level UI in Console to enable frugality mode (tracked ENG-2040). - Add automated regression reporting per prompt family (ENG-2065). - Long-run telemetry retention policy discussion (SRE). Risk assessment: Low risk if kept opt-in; medium if enabled globally without careful rollout. Rollback and safety features implemented to mitigate regression risk. Tests included and CI passing. Release note blurb: "Introducing Frugality Mode — opt-in conservative batching/caching defaults, a shadow-runner for safe quant profile validation, and a quant-drift watchdog to protect quality during low-cost rollouts."
